description: Map a working directory to the Kythene project(s) it belongs to, so you can brief and recall for the right project without a human naming it. Pass what you observe: `marker` (verbatim contents of a .kythene file if one exists - authoritative), `git_remote` (the repo's origin URL), and `dir` (the working directory's basename). Returns matches most-confident first, each with `workspace_id`, `project`, `confidence` (high=marker, medium=git remote, low=directory name) and `via`. A repo can map to several projects and a project can span repos, so this is a LIST. It returns nothing rather than guess when no signal matches confidently - do not brief a project it did not return.

dir.description:
dir is the working directory's basename - the weakest signal, used only
 when the marker and remote produce nothing.

gitRemote.description:
git_remote is the origin remote URL of the repo, if any - e.g.
 https://github.com/acme/widgets or git@host:acme/widgets.git. The
 owner/repo and repo name are matched against project names.

marker.description:
marker is the verbatim contents of a .kythene file at the working directory
 root, if the client found one. It names the workspace and project
 explicitly and is authoritative. Format: `key: value` lines, keys
 `workspace` and `project` (workspace optional; an id or name).

name: resolve_project

matches.description:
matches, most confident first. A repo can map to more than one project and
 a project can span repos, so this is a list. Empty when nothing matched
 confidently - briefing the wrong project reads as authoritative, so no
 guess is returned.

confidence.description:
confidence is "high" (an explicit .kythene marker), "medium" (matched the
 git remote's owner/repo or repo name) or "low" (matched the directory name).

project.description: project is the resolved project (tag) name; project_id its tag id.

via.description: via names the signal that matched: "marker", "remote" or "dir".

title: Which project is this directory?
